title: MVP scope trim: consolidate dashboard tiles, defer trace waterfall, and reduce cost breakdown granularity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Context: The Console observability surface is over-scoped for the December MVP. Engineering capacity and the need to ship a robust, small-surface product require targeted cuts. This ticket is the product decision record to apply surgical scope reductions across dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdowns. Goals: preserve key operator workflows (investigate high error routes, identify cost hot-spots) while deferring lower-impact surfaces that add implementation risk and long tail maintenance.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Dashboard surface reduced to a single 'Service Summary' view + two compact tiles (Errors, Cost Summary). All other card types removed or deferred from the MVP.
2) Trace feature scoped to show a list of sampled traces with basic span timeline and quick links to full trace view disabled (deferred). No waterfall aggregation or span-level heatmaps for MVP.
3) Cost breakdown reduced to a two-level rollup: (a) total route cost, (b) top-5 routes by spend. Per-token and per-parameter breakdowns are deferred.
4) Routing for critical routes: ability to pin and inspect one route's latency/cost history for 7d retained. Advanced filtering (by token range, model variant) deferred.
5) Console UX: All removed tiles must display a 'Deferred to future release' placeholder with a link to the backlog.
6) Performance: Summary dashboard must render within 2s for a 1k-route dataset in staging.
7) Documentation: PRD updated and a short rollout guide created for SRE/solutions with details on fallback behaviors.
8) Stakeholder alignment: PM, Design, and Eng approvals recorded in decision_log and sign-off in comments.
notes:
Trade-offs and rationale:
- Why defer trace waterfall: waterfall implementation requires expensive backend aggregations, introduces storage and retention complexity, and risks delaying launch. We preserve trace list + sample view so investigators can still surface failing requests.
- Why reduce cost granularity: per-token chargeback and detailed parameter costing is valuable but orthogonal to initial operator workflows. Aggregated route spend gives immediate actionability for cost optimization.
- UX trade: consolidating cards reduces discoverability for power users; we will add a 'power user' opt-in in future cadence.
- Engineering: ENG prefers this trim because it aligns with current telemetry indexing pipelines and avoids mocking new aggregation endpoints.
- Future re-adds: waterfall, per-token views, model-variant filtering are tracked as follow-ups in backlog (see links).
